ehealthrnaseq: RNA-seq differential expression with Bioconductor

A short (~10 minute) demonstration of an RNA-seq differential expression workflow in Bioconductor, prepared for the eHealth Hub Bioconductor/OMOP hackathon. It is aimed at people who know clinical data models such as OMOP but are new to Bioconductor. It shows how omics data is held in Bioconductor classes, and where clinical variables enter the analysis.

  • Website: https://michaelplynch.github.io/ehealthhub-hackathon-rnaseq/
  • Docker image: ghcr.io/michaelplynch/ehealthhub-hackathon-rnaseq:latest
  • Vignette: vignettes/rnaseq-demo.Rmd

What the demo covers

Using TCGA clear cell renal cell carcinoma (TCGA-KIRC) tumours and matched adjacent normal kidney:

  1. Getting the data: STAR gene counts from the NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC) via TCGAbiolinks, returned as a RangedSummarizedExperiment.
  2. The SummarizedExperiment class: how assays (counts), rowData()/rowRanges() (genes) and colData() (samples and clinical data) stay aligned when you subset.
  3. Differential expression with DESeq2: a paired design (~ patient + condition) that compares each tumour with the same patient’s normal tissue, with a PCA quality check and apeglm log fold change shrinkage.
  4. Checking the biology: clear cell tumours usually lose VHL, so hypoxia (HIF) targets such as CA9, NDUFA4L2, VEGFA and EGLN3 should be strongly up in tumour.
  5. Visualisation: per-patient CA9 plot, volcano plot and heatmap of the top genes.

Data

The vignette runs on a small cached subset, so it doesn’t depend on the GDC being available:

Project TCGA-KIRC (open access)
Samples 10 patients, each with a primary tumour and a solid tissue normal sample (20 samples)
Features Protein-coding genes (GENCODE v36)
Assays unstranded raw counts, tpm_unstrand
File inst/extdata/TCGA-KIRC_10pairs_STAR_counts.rds (~2 MB)

Patients are the first 10 paired cases by TCGA barcode. Data are from The Cancer Genome Atlas, obtained through the NCI GDC.

Running the demo

Option 1: Docker (recommended)

The image has R, Bioconductor 3.23, all dependencies and this package installed, with RStudio Server running:

docker run -e PASSWORD=<choose_a_password> -p 8787:8787 ghcr.io/michaelplynch/ehealthhub-hackathon-rnaseq:latest

Open http://localhost:8787, log in as rstudio with your password, and open vignettes/rnaseq-demo.Rmd.

Option 2: Locally

Requires R and Bioconductor (developed against Bioconductor 3.23):

install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
remotes::install_github("michaelplynch/ehealthhub-hackathon-rnaseq",
                        dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE,
                        repos = BiocManager::repositories())

Or clone the repository and render the vignette directly:

rmarkdown::render("vignettes/rnaseq-demo.Rmd")

Changing the data

The vignette’s YAML params control the data. With a cached file present, nothing is downloaded.

Parameter Default Meaning
project "TCGA-KIRC" GDC project to use
n_pairs 10 Number of tumour/normal pairs to download (999 = all, ~70 for KIRC)
data_dir "../inst/extdata" Where the prepared .rds is saved and read (relative to the vignette)
gdc_dir "~/GDCdata" Where raw GDC files are downloaded (keep outside the repo)
refresh false true to ignore the cached file and re-download
fdr 0.05 False discovery rate threshold

For example, to build a larger cached subset:

rmarkdown::render("vignettes/rnaseq-demo.Rmd",
                  params = list(n_pairs = 30, gdc_dir = "/scratch/GDCdata"))

Downloads run in small chunks, so if the GDC drops partway through, re-running fetches only the missing files. Fitting time grows quickly with the number of pairs, because the paired design adds one coefficient per patient.

Repository layout 

├── DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE      R package metadata
├── vignettes/rnaseq-demo.Rmd   the demo
├── inst/extdata/               cached TCGA-KIRC subset
├── Dockerfile                  RStudio image built on bioconductor_docker:RELEASE_3_23
├── _pkgdown.yml                website configuration
└── .github/workflows/          R CMD check, pkgdown site and Docker image build

On every push, GitHub Actions runs R CMD check, deploys the pkgdown site to the gh-pages branch and pushes the Docker image to the GitHub Container Registry. New GHCR images are private by default, so the image’s visibility has to be set to public once in the package settings before others can pull it.
